newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: SOCCER-MARADONA GIVES EVIDENCE ABOUT PARTY IN COCAINE CASE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MARADONA GIVES EVIDENCE ABOUT PARTY IN COCAINE CASE.

text.p: Diego Maradona went before an Argentine judge on Tuesday to give evidence in a drugs case in which the former soccer idol's manager has been indicted for cocaine-dealing and his friends arrested for possession.

The 36-year-old player, who admits his own cocaine habit, was silent and grim-faced as he drove to court to talk about a party at Guillermo Coppola's residence days before police found a pound (500 grams) of cocaine in a flower pot there.
"He will answer their questions," his lawyer said as the unshaven player, dressed in black, took the wheel of his jeep.

The hero of Argentina's 1986 World Cup title is distraught at the arrest about two weeks ago of his 49-year-old manager and close friend for possession of drugs for sale, which could land him a jail sentence of up to 20 years. Maradona's brother-in-law, Gabriel Esposito, and ex-international soccer star Alberto Tarantini were also arrested.
Coppola says the drugs were planted. He told Judge Hernan Bernasconi he left his home during a party a few days before the raid and Maradona and three women partied there until late the next day.

Bernasconi said two of the young women arrested in the case accused Tarantini's girlfriend, Natalia de Negri, of planting the cocaine in the flower pot. But he said, "None of these declarations change Coppola's situation. It's a defence strategy to undermine proceedings."
De Negri accused Coppola's lawyer, Mariano Cuneo Libarona, of "threatening her to change her evidence or he would accuse her of planting the drugs at Coppola's home," the judge said.

The Coppola case is giving the Argentine public a glimpse into the tawdrier side of the jet set, where sports stars and politicians consort with drug dealers and prostitutes. New titillating revelations show the undercover policemen who busted Coppola took their job seriously: the judge said two of the women witnesses spoke of "intimate relations" with them.
"It's a universe of very peculiar people," he said with a smile.

The public also was treated to old footage of Coppola in a nightclub men's room dishing out envelopes. "I saw that too, it's amazing," the judge said. "It's worthless as proof but shows his history as someone in the business for a long time."
The case has embarrassed the government as Coppola was a visitor to President Carlos Menem's home and a friend of his late son Carlitos and his private secretary Ramon Hernandez.

Many blame Coppola for Maradona's drug habit, which earned him a 15-month ban at the U.S. World Cup and new allegations of a switched urine test after a match for Boca Juniors last season. He was also to give evidence in that case on Tuesday.
